LESSON: READING 4.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.2: Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we read silently?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify proverbs and sayings from level readers for comprehension
2. enjoy reading silently and widely for pleasure

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 4.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 4.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify proverbs and sayings from level readers for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to identify proverbs and sayings from level readers for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify proverbs and sayings from level readers for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify proverbs and sayings from level readers for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Enjoy reading silently and widely for pleasure

What this means
In this part you learn to enjoy reading silently and widely for pleasure. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: enjoy reading silently and widely for pleasure.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can enjoy reading silently and widely for pleasure. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify proverbs and sayings from level readers for comprehension)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading to a partner. (skill: enjoy reading silently and widely for pleasure)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify proverbs and sayings from level readers for comprehension.
3. Practise this skill: enjoy reading silently and widely for pleasure.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we read silently?
2. What makes a book interesting to read?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify proverbs and sayings from level readers for comprehension.
5. Be able to: enjoy reading silently and widely for pleasure.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
